tei:titleStmt.tei:title: יחץ (מנהג גרבא)
Liturgical Additions for Yaḥats, in the practice of the Jewish community of Djerba

tei:div.tei:head: Liturgical Additions for Yaḥats, in the practice of the Jewish community of Djerba

tei:l.tei:note: As the prayer leader tears the middle matza into the shape of a vav, they recite:

tei:lg.tei:l: Thus Allah tore the sea into twelve paths —
when our ancestors the children of Israel went out from Egypt,
by the hand of our master and prophet and noble
Moses son of Amram, peace be upon him —
and desired their freeing from that slavery;
thus THEY will free us from this exile,
for the sake of THEIR great and awesome name,
and the children will return to their borders,
amen, thus may it be willed.

tei:l.tei:note: After this, the larger piece, the afiqoman, is wrapped in a cloth napkin. A guest, often the youngest child, puts it on their shoulder, walks at least six feet (four cubits, three meters), and recites:

tei:lg.tei:l: A reminder of our ancestors who left Egypt
with their kneading-troughs bundled in their clothes on their backs.

tei:note.tei:p: Find, Pirkei d’Rebbi Eliezer ch. 42, Avot d’Rav Natan 33:2, Midrash Tehillim 114, Targum Pseudo-Yonatan to Shemos 14:21 and Targum Pseudo-Yonatan Devarim 1:1. –ANV
